title: The Refraction Bench
summary: Bend light through water and glass, refocus a microscope, size a pool escape circle and guide a pulse down a fibre.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can use Snell’s law, apparent depth H/n, the slab shift t(1 − 1/n) and the critical angle sin θc = 1/n to reach each objective, and can say when light is totally reflected in a fibre.

levels.title: Ray from water to glass
levels.adds: Baseline: n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r, and indices found from photographs taken in air tell you the angle between two other media (Ex 9.4).
hints: From each photograph, n = sin 60° divided by the sine of the refracted angle.
At the water–glass boundary use n(water) × sin(incidence) = n(glass) × sin(refraction).
Take the inverse sine on your calculator in degrees.

levels.title: Refocusing on Needle
levels.adds: New idea: a liquid of index n makes an object at depth H appear at H/n; refocus by the change in apparent depth (Ex 9.3).
hints: Apparent depth = real depth divided by the index of the liquid.
Work out the apparent depth for each liquid and take the difference.
A larger index makes the needle look nearer the surface, so the microscope must rise.

levels.title: Pin under a glass slab
levels.adds: Apply it: a slab of thickness t and index n makes an object look t(1 − 1/n) nearer, wherever the slab sits (Ex 9.16).
hints: Each thickness t of glass looks like t/n, so the saving is t − t/n.
Slide the slab in your head: the thickness and the index do not change.
Give the raise in cm and say whether the position of the slab matters.

levels.title: The disc over Glow
levels.adds: New idea: light leaves a surface only within the critical angle, sin θc = 1/n, so a source at depth d lights a circle of radius d tan θc (Ex 9.5).
hints: Light is totally reflected at the surface when the angle of incidence exceeds θc.
The radius of the circle is the depth times tan θc.

levels.title: Pulse in the fibre
levels.adds: Apply it: a ray is guided only if it meets the core–cladding wall beyond the critical angle, which limits the entry angle (Ex 9.17).
hints: Inside the core the ray makes an angle of 90° − r with the wall, where sin i = n₁ sin r.
Total reflection needs cos r ≥ n₂/n₁ at the wall.
The widest entry angle satisfies sin i = √(n₁² − n₂²); if that is above 1, every angle is guided.

misconceptions: A glass slab shifts the image by an amount that depends on where the slab is held
Total internal reflection happens when light goes from a rarer to a denser medium
An object under water appears deeper than it is
